statement: For an n-dimensional random vector X = (X_1, ..., X_n)^T with mean μ_X = E[X], the covariance matrix is K_XX = var(X) = E[(X - μ_X)(X - μ_X)^T], an n×n matrix whose (i,j) entry is cov(X_i, X_j) (so the diagonal holds the individual variances).

symbols.meaning: constant real-valued vectors used to form linear combinations of X

properties.why: expanding the defining expectation of the centered outer product
basic property listed directly under the definition

properties.property: K_XX is positive-semidefinite: a^T K_XX a >= 0 for all a in R^n
properties.why: a^T K_XX a = E[(a^T(X - μ_X))^2] >= 0, since it is the variance of a scalar random variable

properties.property: Every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix M is itself a covariance matrix: if var(X) = I then var(M^{1/2} X) = M
properties.why: converse of positive-semidefiniteness, constructed via the symmetric square root M^{1/2} from the spectral theorem

properties.property: For constant matrix A and vector a: var(AX + a) = A var(X) A^T
properties.why: linear transformation rule for the covariance matrix

properties.property: For a same-dimension random vector Y: var(X+Y) = var(X) + cov(X,Y) + cov(Y,X) + var(Y)
properties.why: bilinearity of covariance extended to vector sums

properties.property: Joint covariance of stacked (X,Y) has block form Σ = [[K_XX, K_XY],[K_YX, K_YY]] with K_XY = K_YX^T = cov(X,Y); K_XX, K_YY are the marginal covariance matrices
properties.why: definition of the joint covariance matrix of a stacked random vector

properties.property: As a bilinear form, d^T Σ c = cov(d^T X, c^T X), so c^T Σ c is the variance of the linear combination c^T X
properties.why: covariance matrix acts as a linear operator mapping combinations of X to their covariances with X

properties.property: For complex random vectors Z, K_ZZ = E[(Z-μ_Z)(Z-μ_Z)^H] (conjugate transpose) is Hermitian positive-semidefinite with real diagonal entries; the related pseudo-covariance matrix J_ZZ = E[(Z-μ_Z)(Z-μ_Z)^T] uses plain transpose and is complex symmetric
properties.why: extension of the real definition to complex-valued random vectors

assumptions.assumption: Each component X_i has finite second moment so that E[(X-μ_X)(X-μ_X)^T] exists entrywise
assumptions.breaks_when: a component distribution is heavy-tailed with infinite variance (e.g. Cauchy-like), leaving entries of K_XX undefined

assumptions.assumption: μ_X = E[X] exists and is used to center X
assumptions.breaks_when: the mean itself does not exist for some component

failure_modes.mode: Reported covariance matrix is not actually positive-semidefinite
failure_modes.signature: negative variance implied for some linear combination c^T K_XX c < 0
failure_modes.cause: numerical error, inconsistent/estimated entries, or the matrix was not built from a genuine random vector's second moments

failure_modes.signature: K_XX has zero eigenvalues, determinant is zero, inverse used in conditioning/whitening formulas does not exist
failure_modes.cause: components of X are exactly linearly dependent, or (for estimated covariances) fewer samples than dimensions

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, the robot_localization nodes (ekf_global and ekf_local) run Extended Kalman Filters to estimate the robot's continuous 15-dimensional kinematic state from odometry and IMU measurements. The covariance matrix represents the uncertainties and cross-correlations between these state variables, determining how the filters balance process dynamics with sensor updates.

concrete.in_your_project: The 15-dimensional robot state random vector [15 x 1], comprising 3D position (x, y, z), orientation (roll, pitch, yaw), linear velocities, angular velocities, and linear accelerations.
The mean state estimate [15 x 1] maintained and tracked by the Extended Kalman Filter.
The 15x15 covariance matrix [15 x 15] representing the estimation error covariance of the state, as well as the process noise and initial state uncertainties.

knobs.means: Initializes the filter's state covariance matrix K_{XX} (15x15), establishing the starting uncertainty for each state variable before sensor measurements are incorporated.
Sets the process noise covariance matrix K_{XX} (15x15), dictating how much uncertainty is added to the state estimate at each prediction step due to unmodeled system dynamics.
Defines the initial state covariance matrix K_{XX} (15x15) for local state estimation, specifying the initial variance and cross-terms for the filter.
Defines the process noise covariance matrix K_{XX} (15x15) for local state estimation, controlling how rapidly state uncertainty grows in the prediction phase.
